correctness.rationale: For C_t:y^5=x(x-1)(x-t), tame degree-5 ramification at 0,1,t,infinity yields genus4 by Riemann–Hurwitz. The four regular 1-forms dx/y²,dx/y³,dx/y⁴,x dx/y⁴ form a basis. Cartier maps the first two to each other with coefficients A(t)=[x^18]f^11=-7 t^4(t-1)^4(t-2)(t+1)(t+9) and B(t)=[x^18]f^7=3(t-2)(t+1)(t+9) mod19, and annihilates the latter two. Fresh symbolic F19 polynomial multiplication verified both identities. Thus only t=2,-1,1/2 (excluding t=0,1) have zero Cartier (rank0,a=4), and every other t has invertible two-dimensional semilinear block (stable p-rank2,a=2). Anharmonic transforms t->1-t,1/t partition all 17 F19 parameters into four orbits; fifth roots of scaling constants exist uniquely in F19, so orbit mates are F19-isomorphic. Fresh exact F361 field enumeration found quadratic point-counts 514 for {2,10,18},354 for {8,12},404 for {3,7,9,11,13,17},424 for {4,5,6,14,15,16}. These distinct F361 counts prove the four orbits are pairwise not F19-isomorphic; the first attains genus4 Hasse–Weil upper bound 514. The algebraic Cartier dichotomy holds over the entire geometric t-family, whereas point-count table concerns only F19 parameters.
